Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  Progressive shortness of breath over weeks, worse in last few days; mild dry cough; new bilateral ankle swelling; known chronic heart failure; prior “small heart attack” ~5 years ago (likely prior MI); ex-smoker (~25 pack-years).  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Father died of myocardial infarction in early 60s; mother with osteoporosis (alive).  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Furosemide (dose/route/frequency not documented); Aspirin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Bisoprolol (dose/route/frequency not documented). No known drug allergies.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Not recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Tobacco: former smoker (~1 pack/day for ~25 years). Alcohol: does not drink. Physical activity: walks to the shops daily; no other exercise recorded. Other substances: not recorded. Occupation: part-time lorry (truck) driver, daytime shifts.  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Not recorded.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Reports worry about worsening symptoms and impact on work; no formal screening or risk assessment recorded.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  Lives alone with two cats; employed part-time; concerned about ability to work if health worsens. Housing/financial stressors not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary/findings: Known chronic heart failure with recent subacute worsening of exertional dyspnea, mild dry cough, and new bilateral ankle edema over a few days. No chest pain, palpitations, fever. Appetite adequate. Prior MI (~5 years ago). Exam described as chest “OK,” oxygen saturation “OK,” BP “OK” (no values).  
- Working diagnosis: Acute decompensation of chronic heart failure (volume overload). Supported by history of CHF, progressive dyspnea, and new bilateral ankle edema; prior improvement on diuretics.  
- Plan:  
  - Increase furosemide to one tablet twice daily for the next few days (exact dose not documented).  
  - Order blood tests: CBC (assess for anemia) and kidney function.  
  - Arrange echocardiogram to assess current cardiac function.  
  - Safety net: return earlier for worsening breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.  
  - Follow-up in 1 week to review symptoms and results.  
- DDx considerations (consistent with DDx model):  
  - Anemia contributing to dyspnea and HF decompensation (medium likelihood): “Run-down” feeling; CBC planned.  
  - Arrhythmia (e.g., atrial fibrillation) precipitating HF decompensation (medium-low likelihood): common HF trigger; patient denies palpitations; pulse/rhythm not documented.  
  - Pulmonary embolism (low likelihood): sedentary job risk factor but gradual onset, bilateral edema, and normal O2 sats argue against.  
- Conflict noted: None between transcript and DDx.

- Acute decompensated chronic heart failure (High): Known CHF with progressive dyspnea and new bilateral ankle edema; prior response to diuretics.  
- Anemia contributing to dyspnea/HF decompensation (Medium): “Run-down” feeling; clinician ordered CBC to evaluate.  
- Arrhythmia (e.g., atrial fibrillation) precipitating HF decompensation (Medium-Low): Common HF trigger; no palpitations reported and vitals “OK,” but rhythm not documented.
